newsitem.title: MEXICO: U.S. Treasury's Summers sees Mexico growth rebound.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Treasury's Summers sees Mexico growth rebound.

text.p: Deputy U.S. Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers on Monday said Mexico's economy should be able to achieve economic growth of five percent or more, and he saw an upturn already in real wages.

"There is no reason why Mexico should not grow by the five percent or more the government has targetted -- and every reason for it to try to do so," Summers said in the prepared text of a speech to be delivered to the American Chamber of Commerce in Mexico.
He expected growth would have an impact on Mexican real pay packets this year, noting that "real wages are already heading upward."

Mexico suffered an economic crisis in 1994-5 and was bailed out when on the verge of financial collapse by the United States. Recently the economic recovery has kicked into gear, and Summers said Mexico has put crisis "well behind it".
But he cautioned that Mexico should not over-rely on foreign capital to fuel further growth.

"The trouble...is that if Mexico relies too heavily on foreign capital to finance its growth ambitions, that growth will be vulnerable to the vagaries of market confidence -- and other market factors beyond Mexico's control. The only sustainable way to faster growth is growth in the savings available at home."

He also warned investors not to be over-confident. "There will be the continuing concern that the markets are again buying into a happy ending to the Mexican story before it has really been written," he said.

"That uncertainty, and Mexico's vulnerability to a change of mood, makes it all the more important for it to continue to show that market-led growth and democratic institutions are complimentary goals, not conflicting ones," Summers said.
